result.summary: Adds CreateMultisigDescriptor(), a new internal function that builds a validated, ranged, multipath wsh(sortedmulti(...)) descriptor (with an experimental tr()/sortedmulti_a path) from a threshold and a list of xpub key expressions, rejecting private keys, missing origin info, extra derivation, and duplicates. It is covered by unit tests but has no RPC or GUI caller yet. It is part of the tracked multisig wizard backend effort (#35645).
result.problem: Multisig wallet setup flows currently build descriptor strings via manual bash interpolation with no validation of key form, duplicates, or threshold, which risks malformed or unsafe descriptors for users setting up multisig wallets.

open_concerns: Sjors (maintainer): Concept NACK unless this lands as part of an end-to-end flow with a real consumer (GUI or RPC); believes a Python utility should come first and C++/RPC surface should follow and be shaped by that utility.

Author asked if adding an RPC in this same PR would resolve the concern; Sjors's reply ('Yes, but... I think that's the better yes') leans toward the Python-first sequencing without a final resolution.

result.card: This PR adds CreateMultisigDescriptor(), a C++ helper that builds a validated, ranged, multipath wsh(sortedmulti(...)) (and experimental taproot) descriptor from cosigner xpubs, intended as backend for a future multisig setup wizard (#35645). It replaces ad hoc bash string interpolation with checks for private keys, missing origin info, extra derivation, and duplicate keys, and is covered by unit tests, but has no RPC or GUI caller yet. Maintainer Sjors gave a Concept NACK unless the change ships as part of an end-to-end consumer flow, suggesting a Python utility should come first with C++/RPC support following; the author's follow-up question got an inconclusive reply. The PR is draft, needs rebase, and the maintainer's sequencing question has gone unanswered for 14 days, so review risk is high until the design direction is settled.
